claim_scope: Exact pinned public source and its named defconfig, not the running kernel, a linker map or deployed secure firmware.

adapter_definition.claim: emi_reg_rw.c provides the single inspected definition, selected as emi_reg_rw.o by the EMI Makefile under the parent EMI_MPU gate. The named public defconfig enables that gate and MTK_PSCI, identifies MT6797 and ARM64, and selects the mt6797 platform include path.
adapter_definition.boundary: This is source/build-selection evidence for the named defconfig, not a compiled object or proof that the deployed kernel uses it. The definition's non-PSCI zero-return branch is conditional, not a second selected definition.
adapter_definition.unresolved: Whole-kernel link uniqueness, effective configuration changes and deployment equivalence were not inspected.
adapter_definition.next_discriminator: If deployment attribution becomes necessary, admit a separate exact running-kernel/configuration identity check; this source result alone cannot supply it.

secure_call_mapping.claim: The PSCI branch returns emi_mpu_smc_set(start,end,region_permission), whose MT6797 macro invokes mt_secure_call with function identifier 0x82000209 followed by start, end and packed region_permission. The ARM64 function assigns these respectively to x0, x1, x2 and x3 and issues SMC #0.
secure_call_mapping.boundary: The literal is 0x82000209 even in the ARM64 function; the function's comment is not permission to substitute 0xc2000209. Start/end remain u64 arguments; the unsigned packed word is promoted into x3. No parameter/range validation or ownership acquisition is added in this adapter.
secure_call_mapping.unresolved: Current firmware acceptance of that function identifier and layout is not established by this source audit.
secure_call_mapping.next_discriminator: Any proposed runtime connection must separately establish current firmware compatibility and admitted ownership; no secure call is authorized here.

adapter_return_semantics.claim: The raw ARM64 result is the updated x0-bound u64 variable. mt_secure_call explicitly converts it to int and returns that int; the selected adapter directly returns it without errno remapping. The outer EMI wrapper ignores the adapter result and returns its own zero.
adapter_return_semantics.boundary: The explicit narrowing is the vendor signed-int/low-word boundary; the full raw 64-bit value is not retained by the adapter interface. This audit does not turn the source cast into a portable-C implementation, validate inline-assembly compiler behavior, or infer successful hardware configuration from any zero. Without either PSCI option, the adapter's fallback returns zero without making the call.
adapter_return_semantics.unresolved: Actual runtime raw values, compiler-generated object behavior and correct recovery from denied/failed policy changes remain outside this source attribution.
adapter_return_semantics.next_discriminator: A separately reviewed provider must preserve raw status and handle the signed low word under its accepted ABI contract; this item neither changes the vendor wrapper nor selects that provider.

region18_end_to_end.claim: The frozen WLAN requester passes literal region18 and its first-half-MiB bounds to the outer wrapper. That wrapper masks permissions to 24 bits and carries region18 in bits31:27 (0x90000000), passing original start/end and the packed word to the selected adapter. The adapter/macro put that packed word in x3 for identifier 0x82000209, while the lower returned int is discarded by the outer wrapper.
region18_end_to_end.boundary: End-to-end describes source argument flow and the lost-status boundary, not secure-firmware execution, current region ownership or successful programming. Both predecessor region18 requests use this path. No firmware implementation, lock state, master/domain assignment, selector state or deployed configuration was re-established.
region18_end_to_end.unresolved: All physical/runtime authority and the other CONSYS ownership predicates remain unresolved by this item.
region18_end_to_end.next_discriminator: Use the owning roadmap and a separately admitted owner contract for any future runtime work; there is no remaining adapter-source gap in this bounded chain.
